extract:
Parannoul is the anonymous one-person project of a young musician from Seoul, South Korea, who emerged in the early 2020s as a central figure in a loose online network of Korean bedroom shoegaze and indie rock. Working outside any established local scene and revealing almost nothing about their identity, the artist recorded at home with modest equipment, programmed drums and vocals buried deep in the mix. Their releases spread first through Bandcamp and online music communities such as Rate Your Music before reaching a wider international audience.

The project's formative influences are worn openly. Parannoul has drawn heavily on Japanese alternative rock and emo-leaning guitar music, on the swirling textures of shoegaze, and on the melancholic coming-of-age atmosphere of Japanese film and anime. Shunji Iwai's All About Lily Chou-Chou is a frequently cited touchstone. Their earlier record, Let's Walk on the Path of a Blue Cat, already showed the core approach: plaintive, half-spoken Korean vocals layered over walls of distorted guitar, with lyrics preoccupied by loneliness, failure and adolescent longing.

The breakthrough came with To See the Next Part of the Dream in 2021. The album pairs crushing, lo-fi guitar noise with sentimental melodies, and opens with the sprawling Beautiful World. It became a word-of-mouth phenomenon, and its self-deprecating accompanying notes, in which the artist professed little confidence in the music, became part of its mythology. The record was subsequently picked up for physical reissue by the American label Topshelf Records, while the Korean label Poclanos became an important home for the artist's work. That same year Parannoul appeared on Downfall of the Neon Youth, a split release with fellow Korean bedroom artist Asian Glow and the Brazilian project sonhos tomam conta. The split underscored the transnational, internet-born community surrounding this sound.

Parannoul's collaborative ties deepened with Paraglow in 2022, a joint record with Asian Glow. A steady stream of smaller releases followed, including White Ceiling / Black Dots Wandering Around, Into the Endless Night and Insomnia, which explored more ambient and nocturnal directions. We Shine at Night continued that thread before the arrival of After the Magic in 2023, the most ambitious full-length to date. That album moved away from the deliberately rough production of the breakout record toward fuller arrangements, cleaner recording and grander, almost cinematic swells, while keeping the emotional directness of the earlier work. The live document After the Night (Live), released the same year, marked a shift for a project once defined by its bedroom isolation.

Critically, To See the Next Part of the Dream drew enthusiastic coverage from international outlets and became one of the most discussed independent records of 2021 online. It is often credited with sparking wider global interest in Korean shoegaze and in artists such as Asian Glow and Weatherday-adjacent bedroom acts. Parannoul's success helped show that home-recorded, non-English guitar music could find an audience abroad without traditional promotion, and inspired many imitators in the online shoegaze revival.

The project has remained prolific. In 2024 Parannoul issued a cluster of releases, including Gold River, Lullaby for a Memory, Scattersun, Painless and Sky Hundred, continuing to oscillate between noisy guitar catharsis and softer, more ambient pieces. Still largely faceless, Parannoul stands as one of the defining voices of 2020s internet shoegaze and a key reference point for Korean indie rock's international visibility.
title: Parannoul
